idiographic

Idiographic analysis studies one person at a time. Each person contributes a time series of repeated observations, and a model fitted to that series estimates the effects within that person, for example how a learner’s effort on a day depends on the learner’s self-efficacy on that day. Nomothetic analysis estimates effects averaged over a population of persons. The average describes an individual only when all persons share the same process. Intensive longitudinal data, such as experience sampling (ESM), ecological momentary assessment (EMA) and daily diaries, contain enough observations per person to estimate the process of each person and to examine this assumption.

The package covers two families of idiographic methods. Person-specific statistical models describe the series of each person, regress an outcome on predictors within each person, predict later observations from earlier ones, and separate within-person from between-person effects. Dynamic network models estimate the temporal and contemporaneous relations among several variables, for one person, for each person in a sample, or for the average person in a multilevel model. In both families the person-specific estimates are compared with a pooled model of all persons and with models of subgroups of persons.

Installation

The released version is on CRAN.

install.packages("idiographic")

The development version contains the person-specific statistical models. It is available as a binary from the r-universe of the author and as source from GitHub.

install.packages("idiographic",
                 repos = c("https://mohsaqr.r-universe.dev",
                           "https://cloud.r-project.org"))

pak::pak("mohsaqr/idiographic")

Data

The examples use srl, a data frame in long format with one row per student and day. Thirty-six students rated nine indicators of self-regulated learning, among them self-efficacy, planning, monitoring and effort, on each of 156 days. The column name identifies the student and day orders the observations. The package also contains esm_srl, momentary ratings from 41 students with several occasions per day, and submissions, a simulated daily binary outcome for 40 learners of two latent types.

Person-specific models

A person-specific regression fits one model to the series of each person, and a pooled regression fits one model to the observations of all persons. With scope = "both", fit_lm() estimates both, and metrics() reports their prediction error on the last observations of each person, which are held out from estimation.

library(idiographic)

fit <- fit_lm(srl, y = "effort", x = "efficacy", id = "name", time = "day",
              scope = "both")
metrics(fit, overall = TRUE)
coefs(fit, scope = "individual")

A coefficient estimated from a short or noisy series is uncertain. Empirical-Bayes shrinkage moves each person’s coefficient toward the pooled coefficient, and it moves an uncertain coefficient further than a precise one.

shrink_coefs(fit, term = "efficacy")

A predictor varies within persons, from day to day around the mean of the person, and between persons, in the means themselves. The within-person effect and the between-person effect are estimated in one model, and their difference is the contextual effect.

wb <- fit_within_between(srl, y = "effort", x = "efficacy", id = "name",
                         time = "day")
contextual(wb)

Prediction models from machine learning are evaluated in the same way, on observations later than those used for estimation, and fit_rolling() repeats the evaluation at successive time points.

ml <- fit_ml(srl, y = "effort", x = c("efficacy", "planning", "monitoring"),
             id = "name", time = "day", scope = "both",
             model = c("ridge", "knn"), tune = TRUE)
metrics(ml, overall = TRUE)

Dynamic networks

A dynamic network of several variables has two layers. A temporal edge from one variable to another is the effect of the first variable on one occasion on the second variable on the next occasion. A contemporaneous edge is the partial correlation of two variables on the same occasion after the temporal effects are removed. The multilevel vector autoregression (mlVAR) estimates both layers for the average person, together with a between-person network of the person means.

net <- fit_mlvar(srl, vars = c("efficacy", "planning", "monitoring", "effort"),
                 id = "name", beep = "day")
net
edges(net)
plot(net, layer = "temporal")

Functions

Task Functions
Description of each person describe_persons(), correlate_persons(), variance_components()
Preparation of the panel preprocess_panel(), split_levels(), preprocess()
Regression fit_lm(), fit_glm()
Within-person and between-person effects fit_within_between(), contextual(), correlate_levels()
Prediction and temporal validation fit_ml(), fit_rolling(), compare_predictions()
Pooling and shrinkage pool_coefs(), shrink_coefs()
Subgroups of persons test_subgroups(), find_subgroups(), fit_subgroups()
Treatment effects and heterogeneity fit_effects(), fit_heterogeneity()
Vector autoregression for one person or each person fit_var(), fit_var_each(), fit_graphical_var(), fit_graphical_var_each()
Multilevel vector autoregression fit_mlvar(), fit_mlvar_mplus()
Bayesian vector autoregression and DSEM fit_var_bayes(), fit_mlvar_bayes()
Structural equation models of the series fit_usem(), fit_gimme()
Time-varying networks fit_rolling_var(), fit_rolling_graphical_var()
Stability and forecast validation estimate_stability(), validate_forecast(), compare_idiographic()

Each result is returned as a data frame by as.data.frame(). The accessors metrics(), predictions(), coefs(), importance() and diagnostics() return the parts of a statistical model, and edges(), nodes() and matrices() the parts of a network.

Validation

The estimators are implemented in R and are tested against reference implementations. The table lists the reference for each estimator and the largest difference allowed in the tests.

Estimator Method Reference Agreement
fit_graphical_var() Graphical VAR with graphical lasso and EBIC graphicalVAR within 1e-6 over the supported lag-1 options
fit_mlvar() Multilevel and person-specific VAR mlVAR 0.7.3 within 1e-8 on 20 ESM panels
fit_gimme() Group and individual uSEM path search gimme 10.0 identical paths and matrices on panels of two and three variables, fit indices within 5e-5
fit_mlvar_bayes() Bayesian multilevel VAR (DSEM) Mplus DSEM, Stan, JAGS within Monte Carlo error
fit_var_bayes() Bayesian VAR(1) Mplus with ESTIMATOR = BAYES within 0.02 to 0.03

fit_mlvar_bayes() estimates the two-level Bayesian VAR of Mplus, with latent centring of the person means, by a Gibbs sampler written in R. Its comparison with Mplus covers bivariate models with fixed effects, a univariate model with a random autoregression, and simulations of parameter recovery. equivalence() returns the tested configurations for a fitted model, and equivalence_table() and argument_coverage() return them for all methods.

Dependencies

The package imports only packages distributed with R. The suggested packages lme4 and lavaan estimate the frequentist multilevel VAR and the uSEM and GIMME models, cograph plots the networks, and MplusAutomation connects to a licensed installation of Mplus. Each suggested package is loaded when a function that needs it is called.

The articles at https://pak.dynasite.org/idiographic/articles/ work through each method on the bundled data.
